title: BEAM-ME: Ein interdisziplinärer Beitrag zur Erreichung der Klimaziele
contribution: German outreach article in the GOR magazine OR News (read as the submitted draft) on the BEAM-ME consortium, which moved energy-system LPs onto distributed-memory supercomputers by extending the open-source solver PIPS-IPM with linking constraints and GAMS with block annotation; it reports no computational result (draft pp. 2–4).
problem_entry: Application pressure, not a literature gap: energy-transition planning makes the LP models too large for standard hardware, and the usual LP solvers ran on shared memory only (draft pp. 1–3).
key_idea: Extend PIPS-IPM (block-diagonal LPs with linking variables) by linking constraints, run one process per block holding only its data, and let modellers annotate the block structure of existing GAMS models (draft pp. 3–4).
assumptions: Pure LPs, block-diagonal with linking variables and constraints, blocks from the time index (365 day blocks, or 730 for days and nights); needs a suitable block-diagonal structure; no integer variables, MIP or Benders in the text (draft pp. 2–5; full-text search).
proof_devices: One process per block holding only that block's data (draft p. 3)
Linking constraints added to PIPS-IPM as a solver extension (draft p. 3)
Block structure declared by the modeller through annotation of decision variables in GAMS (draft p. 4)
Named trade-off: enough blocks for parallelism without the linking part dominating (Fig. 3 caption, draft p. 4)
experiments: none: no test set, baseline or number for any computational result; qualitative claims only (draft pp. 3–5)
positioning: Set against the earlier state of energy system analysis and shared-memory LP solvers; no references; an international advisory circle is named (draft pp. 2, 4–5).
writing: Popular magazine register: policy dates and rhetorical questions up front, quantity words where S098 names models and numbers, two candid hedges (core-hour cost, reach not yet assessable) (draft pp. 1, 3–5).
limits_future: Limits printed without counts: block structures suit the algorithms unequally, the annotation trade-off, participants without a suitable structure do not yet benefit, reach open; no next steps. The draft dates the project 2015–2019, the S098 title page 1 Nov 2016 to 30 Jun 2019 (draft pp. 1, 4–5; S098 p. 1).

method_links.note: limits printed but uncounted and without a follow-up project; how many model-experiment participants do not benefit is left open; S098 names models (S098 pp. 21, 37–39 per the s04 card)

step 4 reversed: the missing capability (distributed memory) comes from adopting and extending a foreign open-source solver, not from importing a mechanism into SCIP or SoPlex (as classified for S046 in s02); work with its developers not stated

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: generic over tailored for a heterogeneous user base
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: a general methodology rather than a special case, open to models not based on REMix, tried by six outside institutions on their own models; third card after S098 and S027 (s04), but all from the same consortium and not attributable to Gleixner

transferable: Derive the block granularity from the model's index structure (per day, or per day and night) and check alternative annotations on nonzero plots: more blocks give more parallelism but a larger linking part (draft p. 4, Fig. 3)

Let the modeller declare the decomposition by annotating the decision variables of an existing model instead of rewriting it (draft p. 4); S046 also annotates constraints redundantly for checking (S046 p. 5, s02 card)
Report the core-hours next to the wall time that distributed computing saves; qualitative here (draft p. 3), with numbers in S033 (b02 card, S033 pp. 104–105)
Test generality in a model experiment where outside groups try the method on their own models, and count who does not benefit and why, unlike here (draft pp. 4–5)
coauthors: Thomas Breuer (JSC); Michael Bussieck, Frederik Fiand (GAMS); Karl-Kiên Cao, Hans Christian Gils, Manuel Wetzel (DLR); Thorsten Koch, Daniel Rehfeldt (ZIB/TU Berlin); Dmitry Khabi (HLRS); Gleixner seventh of ten, grouped by institution, no contribution statement (draft p. 1)
